summary: A BBN notice extending the weekly scheduled window for releasing new IMP software from one hour to two, now 7am to 9am Eastern on Tuesdays, because the network had grown to about forty IMPs. The window is always reserved even if not always used. It updates RFC 381 and RFC 406.

plainLanguage.summary: BBN extends the time reserved for weekly IMP software maintenance from one hour to two. The change responds to the larger number of IMPs that must receive software updates.

subtitle: A longer weekly window for scheduled IMP software maintenance.

tldr.problem: As the network grew to about forty IMPs, BBN could no longer complete a system release during the one-hour Tuesday window.
tldr.mechanism: The scheduled software-maintenance period is extended to 7 a.m. through 9 a.m. Eastern time every Tuesday, starting the first Tuesday in February.
tldr.outcome: Hosts are to receive a type 2 IMP-to-Host maintenance message about an hour before a period that will be used. The unit metadata says the RFC updates RFCs 381 and 406.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 440 as Unknown and says it updates RFC 381 and RFC 406. It records a scheduled maintenance change for 1973.

sections.title: Why the Window Is Extended
sections.content:
BBN says scheduled software releases are intended to minimize disruption. The previous Tuesday window ran from 7 a.m. to 8 a.m. Eastern time.

With the network grown to about forty IMPs, BBN could no longer complete a system release to all IMPs in that one-hour period.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN needed more time to update software on all the IMPs. The previous one-hour window was no longer enough.

sections.title: The New Tuesday Window
sections.content:
The scheduled software-maintenance period is extended to two hours, from 7 a.m. until 9 a.m. Eastern time every Tuesday morning. The extension takes effect on the first Tuesday in February.

As before, the period is reserved every Tuesday but will not necessarily be used every week.
sections.plainLanguage: Two hours are now reserved for software maintenance every Tuesday morning. BBN may leave the window unused when no release is needed.

sections.title: Notice to Hosts
sections.content:
On a Tuesday when the maintenance period will be used, Hosts receive a type 2 IMP-to-Host message about an hour before the period. The RFC identifies it as an IMP-GOING-DOWN-FOR-SCHEDULED-SOFTWARE-MAINTENANCE message.

BBN notes that the maintenance period cannot continue to grow linearly with the number of IMPs and says it will find another approach before releases require 168 hours per week.
sections.plainLanguage: Hosts receive an advance message when a scheduled software window will be used. BBN also recognizes that continually lengthening the window would not work indefinitely.

references.text: RFC 381, which describes the scheduled IMP software maintenance procedures.
RFC 406, an earlier reminder about the scheduled IMP software window.
